page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc8i.large is a compute-oriented virtual server belonging to the high-clock-speed ecs.hfc8i instance family. Built on the KVM hypervisor and x86_64 CPU architecture, this instance supplies 2 dedicated vCPUs driven by an Intel Xeon 6462C processor running at a base frequency of 3.3 GHz. The compute cores are paired with 4.0 GB of system memory, providing a tight 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core designed primarily for computation-centric tasks rather than memory-heavy environments.

Network connectivity is provisioned with a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps. The instance includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating VPC-level network configuration or attached elastic IPs for external routing. There is no bundled local storage, meaning primary disk operations and operating system volumes rely entirely on attached cloud storage solutions.

From an efficiency perspective, the dedicated 3.3 GHz CPU allocation eliminates noisy-neighbor CPU throttling, providing consistent clock cycles for workloads sensitive to single-thread latency. Because the configuration carries zero local disks and a compact 4.0 GB memory footprint, resource waste is minimized for compute-focused services that do not require excessive memory allocation.

Hardware tradeoffs center around memory density and storage architecture. The 4.0 GB total RAM capacity limits deployment to workloads that fit into small working sets, while the absence of integrated NVMe or local disk drives requires external block storage for data persistence. Alibaba Cloud ecs.hfc8i.large is well aligned for lightweight compute-bound processing, web serving frontends, continuous integration build workers, API gateways, and microservices requiring dedicated high clock frequencies.
